author: potuz
content:
I don't care about the type of txs, I assume that running KECCACK in a loop would be the most CPU consuming? Maria, Carlos and Toni would be perhaps the right ones to ask. What I want to test is how does the chain attest when payloads finish executing **after** the PTC has voted available, and even better if we can  make them cross into the next slot cause that **should never** happen. 

That is, just to make it clear, a very patological case is a payload that is voted early by the PTC and at the same time does not finish executing until the next slot.

author: potuz
content:
A little update on the Gloas Circuit breaker, I'm opening the first PR now with the single-builder ban (not yet dealing with relays to make it easier to review). I wanted to point out that a short term ban on first offenses and a longer term ban on second has as a very nice corollary that the free option problem can' t really be exercised without some obscure endpoint-sybil mechanisms. I however leave open the door to quickly self heal by also being aggressive in whitelisting: a single block from that banned builder will whitelist it. I think this makes sense because we mostly want to cover ourselves from bugs. But the caveat of this is that 1) this depends on a large chunk of validators actually following a similar design and 2) won't prevent bugs in which a builder may be failing many blocks often but not all.
